knowledge_graph.title: Hib vaccine
knowledge_graph.description: The Haemophilus influenzae type B vaccine, also known as Hib vaccine, is a vaccine used to prevent Haemophilus influenzae type b infection. In countries that include it as a routine vaccine, rates of severe Hib infections have decreased more than 90%.

text_blocks.snippet: The Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) vaccine is a vaccine used to prevent Haemophilus influenzae type b infection. It's particularly important for children under 5, as Hib disease can be severe. The vaccine is also recommended for older children and adults in certain high-risk situations.
snippet_highlighted_words: The Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) vaccine

text_blocks.snippet: Key points about the Hib vaccine:

list.title: What it protects against:
list.snippet: The Hib vaccine protects against invasive Hib disease, which can cause serious illnesses like meningitis, pneumonia, and epiglottitis.

list.title: Who should get it:
list.snippet: The CDC recommends Hib vaccination for all children under 5 years old. It is also recommended for older children and adults in specific situations, such as those with weakened immune systems, those who have had their spleen removed, or those with sickle cell disease.
